title: Energy-Energy Correlators at Strong Coupling
abstract: We study energy-energy correlators (EEC) in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory at strong 't Hooft coupling $\lambda$. We consider the EEC in states created by half-BPS operators of arbitrary dimension $p$, and determine the corresponding event-shape function up to order $\lambda^{-3/2}$ from the worldsheet representation of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude with Kaluza-Klein external states. For $p=2$ we compute the second curvature correction, which completes the EEC through order $\lambda^{-2}$; the new contribution improves the agreement with recently derived non-perturbative bounds at intermediate coupling. We further develop a complementary method in which the strong-coupling expansion coefficients of the EEC are extracted directly from the Wilson coefficients of low-energy expansion of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude, and find the two approaches in perfect agreement.

title: Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments
abstract: We present a combined analysis of the latest publicly available atmospheric neutrino data from Super-Kamiokande including all data-taking stages previous to the gadolinium phase, IceCube-DeepCore, and the six-detection-unit configuration of KM3NeT/ORCA. Our fit uses all event samples simultaneously and treats the systematic uncertainties shared among experiments as fully correlated, while detector-response uncertainties are modeled independently for each experiment. %We measure The combined data constrain the atmospheric oscillation parameters to $\Delta m^2_{31} = 2.44^{+0.06}_{-0.04} \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$ and $\sin^2\theta_{23} = 0.52^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$, with a precision of $2.2\%$ and $6.1\%$, respectively, which is competitive with current accelerator-based measurements, and independently constrain the $CP$-violating phase to $\delta_{CP} = 1.30^{+0.24}_{-0.28}~\pi$. Finally, comparing the orderings of the neutrino mass spectrum, we find a preference for the normal ordering with $\Delta\chi^2 = 11.0$; further calibrated with pseudoexperiments, we exclude the inverted ordering at $99.95\%$ confidence level ($3.3\sigma$).

title: Energy-energy correlators in the large-charge limit of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory
abstract: We study the energy-energy correlator (EEC) in heavy states of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory in the large-charge 't Hooft limit, in which the dimension $\Delta$ of the heavy operator (or, equivalently, its $R$-charge) is taken to infinity with the effective coupling $\lambda_Q \propto g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2\Delta$ held fixed. The relevant heavy-heavy-light-light four-point correlators are known to all orders in $\lambda_Q$ in this limit. For certain classes of operators, the perturbative series can be resummed to obtain exact finite-coupling expressions. We use these results to determine the corresponding EEC, whose dynamical part can be extracted from a double discontinuity of the four-point correlator. We determine the EEC at finite effective coupling and study its physical behavior as a function of $\lambda_Q$ and the angular separation between the detectors, both at generic angles and in the collinear and back-to-back limits.

title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the QFT-natural prescription in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem $\,$---$\,$ which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system $\,$---$\,$ is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.

title: Aspects of Anomalies: Fermion Family Constraints, Gravitational Form Factors and Scattering Amplitudes
abstract: Quantum anomalies play two complementary roles in quantum field theory: as consistency conditions that constrain the field content of a theory, and as dynamical effects encoded in the analytic structure of correlation functions. This thesis explores both. In the first part, we study the 331 model, in which gauge anomalies cancel across families rather than within each one. Combined with QCD asymptotic freedom, this fixes the number of fermion generations to three. We analyze the model's symmetry breaking, scalar and flavor sectors, and its TeV-scale Landau pole. We then study the collider phenomenology of its exotic quarks, showing that the pair production of heavy quarks decaying into doubly-charged vector bileptons gives a clean same-sign dimuon plus b-jets signature, observable at a 100 TeV collider but not at the LHC. Finally, we introduce the left-right symmetric 33311 extension, which preserves the family-number constraint and avoids proton decay. In the second part, we use conformal field theory in momentum space to study the chiral, gravitational and conformal anomalies. We construct a complete off-shell parametrization of the non-Abelian TJJ correlator in perturbative QCD, identifying the dilaton-like anomaly pole. For the AVV, ATT and TJJ vertices, we prove mass-independent anomaly sum rules for the spectral density, showing that the anomaly pole is not an asymptotic particle state. We apply the TJJ insertion to the pion gravitational form factors at large momentum transfer with Sudakov resummation: the anomaly feeds mainly into the D-term and the trace form factor, improving agreement with lattice QCD. Lastly, sewing two anomaly vertices through graviton exchange, we show that the trace anomaly activates a gauge-invariant scalar gravitational channel, giving a double-copy-like structure in photon and graviton scattering.

title: Floquet Instability of Photon-Axion Conversion
abstract: The discovery of axions would provide evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we investigate axion-photon conversion in the presence of a background magnetic field with simultaneous spatial and temporal periodicity. By performing a Lorentz transformation, the coupled axion-photon system is mapped onto a time-periodic linear system that can be analyzed using Floquet theorem. We find unstable modes associated with resonant crossing between Floquet replicas. The resulting complex Floquet exponents lead to exponentially growing modes, which we identify as a Floquet instability. Then, we determine the parameter regions in which this instability appears in a perturbative analysis. We further show that the Floquet instability enhances the axion-field amplitude generated from an initial photon field. Our results demonstrate that spatiotemporally periodic magnetic backgrounds provide a distinct mechanism for modifying axion-photon conversion through Floquet instability.

title: Axion-Like Particle Searches at Muon Colliders: Photon-Neutrino Signatures and Heavy-Neutral-Lepton Feasibility

Five benchmarks spanning $m_a=100$--$1000\GeV$ are generated at $g_{a\gamma\gamma}=0.01\TeV^{-1}$ and flavor-universal pseudoscalar neutrino couplings $y_

Assuming a 1\% background normalization uncertainty, a cut-based photon-line selection gives projected 95\% sensitivity to $g_{a\gamma\gamma}\simeq0.039$--$0.045\TeV^{-1}$ at $3\TeV$ and $0.0137$--$0.0140\TeV^{-1}$ at $10\TeV$. A ROOT/TMVA gradient-boosted decision tree with validation-fixed thresholds reaches held-out AUC values of $0.9967$--$0.9993$ and $g_{95}=0.0192$--$0.0400\TeV^{-1}$ at $3\TeV$ and $0.0122$--$0.0144\TeV^{-1}$ at $10\TeV$. title: $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^{\ast} \ell^+\ell^-$ decays with polarized leptons
abstract: We present an analysis of lepton polarization observables in the rare flavor-changing neutral current decays $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda\ell^+\ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^*\ell^+\ell^-$. These decays are driven by the quark-level transition $b \to s\ell^+\ell^-$ and are sensitive to short-distance physics within and beyond the Standard Model. We work within an effective Hamiltonian framework and derive single lepton polarization asymmetries, double lepton polarization asymmetries, and polarized forward-backward asymmetries using the helicity method. The observables are expressed in terms of transversity amplitudes and evaluated using state-of-the-art lattice QCD form factors. We analyze the $q^2$ dependence of several observables for both the ground-state $\Lambda$ and the excited $\Lambda^*(1520)$ final states and discuss sensitivities of the observables to chiral structure of the effective operators and complex Wilson coefficients.

title: Nonlinear Response of Schwarzschild Black Holes at Arbitrary Perturbative Order
abstract: We establish recursive integration-by-parts identities that symbolically reduce the inhomogeneous solutions of the Regge-Wheeler-Zerilli equation to a small set of master integrals, yielding the nonlinear response kernels of Schwarzschild black holes at arbitrary perturbative order. We further derive a closed ODE system that enables rapid, accurate, and stable numerical evaluation of these master integrals. To demonstrate our result, we compute quadratic, cubic, and quartic quasinormal-mode coupling coefficients as special cases of the response kernels.

title: Nambu-Goldstone Bosons and Quantum Fisher Information
abstract: The quantum Fisher matrix and geometric tensor are powerful tools for quantifying the nature of quantum systems. Unfortunately, the formalism needed to compute these quantities is opaque and has limited the development of physical intuition for their behavior, even in the ground state. For quantum systems with continuous symmetries, we know the ground state can be understood in a model-independent and intuitive way from the correlation functions of conserved currents and charges. In this paper, we demonstrate an equivalence between the quantum Fisher matrix associated with the ground states of systems with continuous symmetries and the Nambu-Goldstone. bosons produced by broken generators. We will show that the information metric defined by the Fisher matrix is the same as the Zamolodchikov metric that defines the coset space of the system. Next we show that the Uhlmann curvature associated with multi-parameter estimation is the same as the charge density matrix that defines the difference between type-A and type-B Nambu-Goldstone bosons. We demonstrate these connections in several examples and discuss the generalization to finite temperature.

title: Annihilation feedback on elastic scattering in self-interacting dark matter
abstract: Sizable dark-matter self-interactions, motivated by observations of galactic structure, often arise from the exchange of light force mediators. Light mediators can render scattering nonperturbative and make inelastic processes important. Unitarity, via the optical theorem, implies that elastic and inelastic interactions cannot be treated independently: inelasticity induces absorptive contributions to the two-particle self-energy kernel that determines the elastic amplitude, while the resulting incoming-state dynamics also modifies the inelastic amplitudes. We study the feedback of dark-matter annihilation on elastic scattering in the presence of a long-range force. Although annihilation is a short-distance process, it can be strongly enhanced by such a force. We find that its feedback becomes significant near Sommerfeld resonances, where it suppresses the low-velocity growth of the baseline elastic cross section. Near baseline elastic-scattering zeros, it may instead generate a nonzero elastic floor required by unitarity. A companion paper studies the feedback of radiative bound-state formation on elastic scattering, which can generate sizable self-interactions.

title: Probing Lepton Flavor Violation at FCC-ee
abstract: We investigate the prospects for probing Lepton Flavor Violation (LFV) at FCC-ee within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) framework. The approximately $2 \times 10^{11}$ $\tau$-lepton pairs expected at the $Z$-pole run of FCC-ee could improve current limits on the branching fractions of $\tau\to3\ell$ and $\tau\to\ell\gamma$ ($\ell=e,\mu$) by factors ranging from 30 to 800, depending on the specific channel. We compare the resulting new-physics reach with that obtained from searches for $Z \to \tau \ell$ and $h \to \tau \ell$, which have so far received greater attention in studies of LFV at future $e^+e^-$ colliders. We find that $\tau$ decays can surpass both the current and the projected sensitivity of $Z\to\tau\ell$ searches to the same LFV interactions, while probing a broader range of SMEFT operators. We further show that, for LFV Yukawa-like interactions, direct searches for $h\to\tau\ell$ provide the strongest sensitivity. By contrast, for semileptonic operators that radiatively induce LFV Higgs decays, this hierarchy can be reversed, with $\tau$ decays providing the leading probe.

title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
abstract: We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. This generates a direct dark matter-dark energy interaction. We show that generic models with a significant dark matter-dark energy coupling suffer from a naturalness problem: the Coleman-Weinberg potential induced by the interaction is typically much larger than the dark energy scale. In our model, the corrections arise from a monodromy tower of dyon states, allowing them to be exponentially suppressed. In the minimal setup, the interaction strength is predicted to be $\sim 0.1\%$, below the sensitivity of current observations. We discuss scenarios in which cosmological population of higher-charge dyons can enhance the interaction to the percent level, producing an apparent phantom dark energy equation of state. We further show that the parameter space of the axion-monopole model preferred by fitting the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) results can also naturally explain the cosmic birefringence with a small anomaly coefficient.

title: LEAF: LUT-aware Efficient Attention on FPGAs
abstract: We introduce Lookup-table (LUT)-aware Efficient Attention on FPGAs (LEAF). LEAF is the first nanosecond-scale LUT-aware transformer for FPGAs. Deploying transformers that are large enough to perform well, small enough to fit on an FPGA, and fast enough to meet the sub-microsecond timescales required by real-time systems such as those at CERN remains difficult, since the same attention mechanism that gives these models their high expressivity also makes them costly to implement in hardware. LEAF converts the query, key, and value projections and the final output feed-forward layer into FPGA-native layers with LUT-aware training, creating the first LUT-aware transformer and linformer layers built for ultra-low-latency inference. Attention resists LUT-aware training because it multiplies two activations where the method needs a constant weight to tabulate; LEAF tabulates the attention block's constant matrix-vector multiplications and leaves the rest in arithmetic form. On a standard jet tagging benchmark this improves accuracy by 1.8 percentage points while using 2.9 times fewer LUTs than the previous state-of-the-art sub-microsecond transformer at the same input size. Our most efficient LEAF-based linformer with 64 input particles reaches 80.4% classification accuracy at 28k LUTs and 35ns.

title: Cosmic birefringence from a stiff axion field and its cosmological implications
abstract: We propose a model in which the observed cosmic microwave background birefringence arises from the interaction of photons with a stiff ($w=1$) pseudo-scalar field that today contributes a subdominant fraction of the total energy density, distinct from both dark matter and dark energy. Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constrains the cosmological density of the stiff field, leading to a lower bound for its coupling with photons, $g_{\phi\gamma} > 8.9 \times 10^{-14}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Photon conversion in cluster-hosted quasars sets an upper bound, $g_{\phi\gamma} < 5.0 \times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Therefore, there is a narrow window for the discovery of this cosmological component that can be explored in the forthcoming years with astrophysical axion searches. Moreover, we show that this scenario leads to gravitational-wave signals that can be tested with planned experiments.

title: Self-interacting dark matter from radiative bound-state-formation feedback
abstract: Observations of galactic structure motivate sizable dark-matter self-interactions at low velocities, naturally realized through light force mediators. Such mediators can also make inelastic processes very efficient. Unitarity then requires their absorptive contributions to the two-particle self-energy kernel to be resummed, which in turn feeds back into both the elastic and inelastic scattering amplitudes. We study the feedback of radiative bound-state formation on elastic scattering and its implications for self-interacting dark matter. We focus on capture processes through emission of a charged scalar; such transitions are particularly efficient because the scattering and bound states are governed by different effective potentials, a feature also shared by radiative capture through emission of a non-Abelian gauge boson. We show that their feedback can generate sizable elastic scattering relevant for halo dynamics, even when the baseline elastic amplitude vanishes. Notably, the generated elastic cross section can grow toward low velocities, resembling long-range scattering. A companion paper examines the feedback from annihilation processes.

title: Combining Pumping and Absorption Effects in Neutrino Oscillation Probabilities: A Non-Hermitian Framework
abstract: We study two-flavour neutrino oscillations in which a coherent off-diagonal interaction from a complex background field coexists with an absorptive channel acting on a single mass eigenstate. Since the two do not commute, the effective Hamiltonian is non-normal and oscillations and damping no longer factorise. We formulate the dynamics both as the no-jump sector of a Lindblad evolution and through biorthogonal diagonalisation, and obtain the evolution operator of our model in closed form. The model interpolates between quasi-global damping, standard invisible decay, and a critical point with polynomial-times-exponential evolution; for initially pure states it describes norm loss rather than decoherence. Comparing neutrinos and antineutrinos in the same background, with the mixing phase $\phi$ reversed and the background phase $\delta$ fixed, we derive closed-form $CP$, $CPT$ and $T$ asymmetries. The $CPT$ asymmetries arise only from this phase assignment. In contrast, the $T$ asymmetry, which is forbidden in unitary two-flavour oscillations, is independent of the prescription: it arises only through the non-normal structure, is proportional to the absorptive coupling, and vanishes only when $\delta+\phi=n\pi$. For equal initial populations the net neutrino--antineutrino asymmetry vanishes identically, while a non-zero flavour asymmetry survives and requires a non-normal Hamiltonian.

title: Two-loop helicity amplitudes for $gg\to W^+W^-$ using high-energy and forward expansions
abstract: We calculate next-to-leading order QCD corrections for the process $gg \to W^+W^-$ with two off-shell $W$ bosons, accounting for virtual top quarks in the loop diagrams. Our approach relies on combining expansions valid in different regions of phase space. Specifically, we perform a high-energy expansion in which the Mandelstam variables are much larger than the top-quark mass. Furthermore, we expand around the forward-scattering limit, where the Mandelstam variable $t$ is small. We also provide an expansion for large top-quark mass, which serves as an important cross-check. We provide technical details regarding the various expansions and demonstrate that precise results are obtained for all helicity amplitudes across the entire phase space. Our results exhibit an explicit dependence on all input parameters.

title: The Electron-Recoil Response Tail and the LZ High-Energy Event Background
abstract: We reconstruct the continuum electron-recoil contribution to the LZ background expectation from the collaboration's released simulation configuration. The released model specifies a definite response tail, but the published calibration information supplies no bound on how far the physical tail may depart from it at the probabilities the expectation depends on. Distributions reproducing the executable model's mean, variance, and standardised skewness exactly, and its event-conditioned 10, 50, and 90\% \(N_e\) quantiles to about one per cent, differ in the relevant tail probability by more than five orders of magnitude. The ladder is short: a tail agreeing with that central characterisation to 0.14\% in the quantiles lifts the electron-recoil contribution out of the negligible range, and one agreeing to 0.47\% makes it comparable to the entire background quoted for the comparison region. We go on to identify the measurements that would settle it.

title: This is SParTA: A modular, efficient and scalable transformer architecture for jet-tagging
abstract: We present the Sparse Particle-interaction Transformer Architecture (SParTA), a modular, scalable, and efficient transformer for jet tagging at high-energy colliders. Exploiting the steeply falling transverse-momentum ($p_T$) spectrum of jet constituents, SParTA factorizes constituent processing into two topological regimes. Ordered by descending $p_T$, only the $N$ hardest constituents (the hard core) participate in quadratic $O(N^2)$ differential interaction attention driven by pairwise physical and learned relational features. The remaining soft constituents are integrated via linear $O(lN)$ cross-attention to the hard core, preserving soft-radiation and color-flow information while avoiding the $O(l^2)$ memory bottleneck of full self-attention over all $l$ constituents. Pairwise interaction features are computed dynamically in-network from constituent four-momenta and conditioned on global jet-level substructure observables. On the quark-gluon tagging benchmark, a 300K-parameter SParTA model achieves an AUC of 92.02% and accuracy of 85.06%, matching the 2.14M-parameter Particle Transformer (ParT) at one-seventh the parameter count and outperforming IAFormer by 21% in background rejection at 30% signal efficiency. On the boosted top-tagging benchmark, SParTA outperforms ParT and ParticleNet with 511K parameters, while we analyze the architectural trade-offs relative to fully dense multi-layer interaction networks.

title: Illuminating Light Dark Matter with Fixed-Target Experiments
abstract: Astronomical and cosmological observations provide overwhelming evidence for a non-luminous matter component, dark matter (DM), whose particle nature remains unknown. Experimental searches for non-gravitational DM interactions have largely targeted DM with GeV-TeV masses via nuclear recoils, yielding no discovery thus far. DM in the MeV-GeV mass range, however, is theoretically motivated, reproducing the observed relic abundance while remaining invisible to nuclear recoil searches. Such light DM is better probed via electron recoils or at fixed-target experiments. This thesis advances the theoretical and statistical toolkit for light DM searches at fixed-target experiments, spanning model building, statistical inference, global fits, and signal simulation. We survey the landscape of fixed-target searches for light DM, focusing on the Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX). We also simulate DM signatures at the next-generation experiment SHiP to assess its sensitivity. Within minimal DM models, we present a likelihood-based statistical framework for LDMX using the full two-dimensional recoil electron distribution, spanning exclusion, discovery, parameter estimation, and model comparison in frequentist and Bayesian formulations. This establishes the discovery potential of LDMX, and we quantify the direct detection exposure needed to independently confirm a potential signal. Beyond this paradigm, we perform global fits of scalar and fermionic light DM, combining cosmological, astrophysical, and laboratory constraints. We then extend fixed-target searches to spin-1 DM and higher electromagnetic moment dark photons, yielding rich signatures with strong complementarity to other probes. Finally, we go beyond standard nuclear modelling of dark photon production, incorporating elastic nuclear form factors and spectral functions from many-body ab initio methods in place of analytic treatments.

title: Jets as differential probes of hot QCD matter
abstract: Ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions create short-lived droplets of deconfined, hot QCD matter whose evolution connects far-from-equilibrium early dynamics to the hydrodynamic quark-gluon plasma. High-energy jets, produced in early hard scatterings and modified by this evolving medium, provide multi-scale probes of its microscopic properties. This thesis develops perturbative QCD tools to extract information about hot QCD matter from its imprint on differential jet substructure observables. Our framework is the BDMPS-Z description of high-energy partons propagating through stochastic colour fields. We first study anisotropic QCD matter by replacing the usual scalar broadening parameter with direction-dependent transverse momentum broadening. This relates anisotropic corrections to medium-induced splittings to spin information and azimuthal patterns in final-state energy flow. Energy correlators are then used as observables sensitive to these effects, including heavy-flavour EECs, azimuthally differential EECs and clover projections designed to isolate leading anisotropy-induced harmonics. We also examine how energy loss affects the interpretation of jet substructure modifications. Quantile matching defines reconstructed energy loss as a population-level shift between vacuum and medium-modified jet spectra. We further develop energy-loss functions, which encode the distribution of energy retained by jet-originated hadrons, and show how their moments enter multi-point projected energy correlators. Finally, we go beyond single $1\to2$ medium-induced splittings by studying spin-induced correlations between successive emissions and higher-point energy correlators including contributions from medium response. The results show that differential jet substructure can probe directional properties of QCD matter and multi-point dynamics of jets propagating through it.

title: Searching for Dense Perturbers in Cold Dark Matter Simulations
abstract: Recently, several low-mass, dense perturbers have been inferred from astrophysical observations of gravitational lensing, stellar streams, and satellite galaxies. If interpreted as dark matter subhalos, their inner densities exceed the predictions of the standard cold dark matter (CDM) model. We systematically investigate this tension using a CDM-only zoom-in simulation of a Milky Way analog. We analyze more than 5000 subhalos with masses down to $10^6\,M_\odot$ and reconstruct their inner density profiles using a tidal truncation model. The simulated subhalos are then compared with the observed compact perturbers in terms of their density profiles, enclosed masses, concentrations, and projected cylindrical masses. None of the simulated CDM subhalos is sufficiently dense to reproduce the inferred mass distributions of the observed perturbers. We further examine the redshift evolution of subhalo concentrations and derive a fitting function to characterize this evolution. Our findings motivate further investigations into exceptionally rare formation histories that could produce such dense perturbers, as well as the possibility of physics beyond the standard CDM model.

title: Correlations in oscillation data and their impact on neutrino mixing models
abstract: With increasing precision of neutrino experiments, complete correlation among the oscillation parameters will scrutinize theoretical neutrino mass and mixing models. Using available 1D--3D global-fit datasets, we construct a multidimensional $\tilde{\chi}^2$ function that provides a conservative estimate of the full six-dimensional parameter correlations. In our approach, we delineate the model-constrained parameter space by combining the interpolated experimental data with the analytical relations implied by a given mixing scheme. We identify $\tilde{\chi}^2_{\text{min}}$, corresponding to the optimal agreement attainable for parameter points satisfying the model. Applying this framework to several schemes ($\text{TM}_{1,2}$, $\mu1,2$--$\tau1,2$) yields generally better fits for IO than for NO, with the $\mu1$--$\tau1$ scheme under IO providing the best overall fit. While $\mu1,2$--$\tau1,2$ and $\text{TM}_1$ schemes perform significantly better than $\text{TM}_2$, the latter is excluded at $>3\sigma$ C.L. using NuFIT~v6.1 data. We further evaluate the implications of these correlation-respecting constraints on the effective neutrino mass observables relevant to tritium $\beta$-decay ($m_{\beta}$) and neutrinoless double $\beta$-decay ($m_{\beta\beta}$). The proposed approach can be readily extended to test any theoretical framework that predicts algebraic relations among neutrino oscillation parameters, and we provide a GitHub starter kit.

title: Double diffraction production for dipole-dipole scattering at high energies
abstract: This paper is a first attempt to describe double diffractive production in dipole-dipole scattering within high energy QCD. Our approach is based on summing large BFKL Pomeron loops, which generate two clusters of hadrons separated by a rapidity gap. Unlike in the BK framework, our approach allows both clusters to carry large masses. We derive the cross section for the production of two such clusters and show that it exhibits geometric scaling. Testing this scaling behaviour against data from high-energy colliders such as the LHC will be a crucial step in establishing whether large Pomeron loops play a major role in high energy QCD dynamics, and in particular in the unitarization of the scattering amplitude.

title: Pretraining on boosted boson decays for polarization tagging of hadronic $W$ bosons
abstract: Longitudinally polarized weak bosons probe the unitarization of vector-boson scattering. At large boosts, longitudinal and transverse $W$ bosons produce jets with the same mass and two-prong structure, distinguished only by the decay angle. Longitudinal bosons are rare: they occur in only 0.3% of $W$+jet events at these large boosts. We ask where the polarization information of a boosted $W$ boson lies and how much a tagger can recover. Requiring both decay quarks within the jet truncates the decay-angle distribution at an edge set by $m/(p_T R)$, which we show bounds any hadronic polarization tagger. Within this acceptance, the decay angle carries essentially all the polarization information of a jet in $W$+jet events. Polarized samples are costly to simulate for vector-boson scattering, so we pretrain a point-edge transformer on $10^7$ unpolarized jets of boosted bosons, top quarks and QCD and test how much it recovers from few labels. Fine-tuned on 783 labeled jets per class with its transformer blocks kept fixed, the network pretrained to classify these jets improves on training from scratch, but generic pretraining on a broad mix of jets and a boosted decision tree on substructure observables do as well. The best taggers recover most, but not all, of the separation the decay angle allows, and student networks with a few hundred times fewer parameters, trained by knowledge distillation, match their teacher. More information lies outside the jet. The production angle, reconstructed with the recoiling jet, improves every tagger. In diboson production and vector-boson scattering at matrix-element level, the production kinematics carry more information than the decay angles of both bosons. Trading the generality of a jet tagger for an event-level tagger trained on the process thus brings significant gains, which measurements of longitudinal vector-boson scattering could exploit.

title: Nonlocality effects on fermions confined within a hard-wall potential
abstract: We investigate nonlocality effects on the energy spectrum of spin-$1/2$ fermions confined by hard-wall potentials. Starting from a nonlocal Dirac theory with a modified kinetic term, we formulate the associated field equation in flat spacetime using cylindrical coordinates. By exploiting the eigenvalue spectrum of the squared Dirac operator, the original infinite-order equation is reduced to a finite-order problem. We also show that on the branch continuously connected to the local Dirac theory the nonlocal corrections can be encoded in an effective fermion mass. We then find analytical energy spectra for two confining geometries: a cylindrical hard wall and a quantum ring defined by two concentric cylindrical boundaries. In both cases, the radial equations reduce to Bessel equations and the boundary conditions quantize the allowed modes. The local hard-wall spectra are recovered for $\Lambda\to\infty$, whereas finite nonlocality shifts the mass contribution and, consequently, the particle--antiparticle energy separation. These results provide a direct characterization of nonlocal effects in quantum-confined fermionic systems.

title: The $b\bar{b}c\bar{c}$ Fully Heavy Tetraquark at the LHC and the FCC: Multimodal Fragmentation and Observability
abstract: We investigate the production of the all-heavy mixed-flavor $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark through a multimodal fragmentation setup combining direct-multiquark and scalar-diquark mechanisms. Standard Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) evolution is applied while preserving threshold consistency through the Heavy-Flavor NonRelativistic evolution (HF-NRevo) scheme. The resulting fragmentation functions (FFs) are then embedded into hybrid high-energy and collinear factorization at next-to-leading order for semi-inclusive tetraquark-plus-jet production. We compare the two mechanisms through rapidity-separation distributions at the 14 TeV High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) and at the 100 TeV Future Circular Collider (FCC), finding a clear phenomenological preference for the direct-multiquark channel over the scalar-diquark mode. Integrated cross sections and expected event yields provide favorable production-level prospects for future searches at the HL-LHC, with substantially enhanced statistics at FCC energies. These results establish a quantitative connection between microscopic formation mechanisms and the prospective observability of the $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark at present and future hadron colliders.

title: Non-Classicality in $tW$ system via negativity and geometric quantum discord
abstract: We perform a phenomenological study of non-classical correlations in the mixed-dimensional qubit-qutrit system realized by leading order $pp\to tW$ production at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV in the leptonic final state. The two missing neutrinos are reconstructed with conditional normalizing flows trained on simulated detector-level objects, and the joint spin density matrix $\rho_{tW}\in\mathcal{H}_2\otimes\mathcal{H}_3$ is obtained in a generalized Bloch representation from the angular distributions of the leptonic decay products. Non-classical correlations are quantified using the Peres--Horodecki negativity and geometric quantum discord. We quantify the correlations at different region of $m_{tW}$ at the reconstruction level within the Standard Model and the impact of two reducible backgrounds viz. $t\bar{t}$ and $WWj$ processes, tagged using boosted decision trees. We further study the behavior of correlations in presence of anomalous chromomagnetic and chromoelectric dipole moments of the top quark. The sensitivity reach of the quantum observables along with polarization and spin correlation parameters are reported for current LHC and future HL-LHC scenario.

title: A Radiation-Hardened, Fault-Aware Quantized Neural Network That Self-Heals
abstract: Deep learning (DL) models are increasingly being deployed into radiation-challenging environments in spacecraft, particle accelerators, and, soon, space-based data centers. Instantiated as a learned orchestration of numbers stored in persistent memory, models are susceptible to continual degradation as high-energy particles corrupt data. At inference time, new data passed through the network fundamentally break the off-line assumptions and guarantees of a static model determined during training. To preserve the quality and efficacy of the models, fault tolerance against bit flips is a clear objective. In this work we developed a runtime method for repairing the quantized weights of neural networks (NNs) after bit flips on commodity, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware, without storing extra replicas. Our work extends the well-established Fault-Aware Training (FAT) paradigm by adding an alignment penalty to concentrate undamaged activations and weights into a low-rank subspace, and we then reconstruct flagged corrupted coordinates from the uncorrupted survivors. We call this method {\it Projection Healing} and apply it to six regression benchmarks on quantized NNs. Holding a FAT checkpoint fixed and toggling only the runtime heal gives a further ${\sim}23\%$ reduction in the native-unit excess integral. Across those datasets the method extends the operational scrub interval by a median of $2.04\times$ at a $+5\%$ RMSE degradation and $1.96\times$ at $+50\%$, compared with $1.62\times$ and $1.07\times$ for classical Single Error Correction, Double Error Detection (SECDED). This introduces a new path towards designing resilient data-driven models, complementing established hardware redundancy, ECC, and FAT-based techniques.

title: Parameter dependence of the mapping of the mean-field Ising model onto QCD in the first-order phase transition regime
abstract: We map the mean-field Ising equation of state onto the QCD phase diagram and investigate how scaling parameters alter the metastable and unstable regions, as well as the symmetrized pressure and density along an isotherm on the QCD $T-\mu_B$ phase plane. We find that, for both the conventional mapping scheme and the scheme valid in the small-quark-mass limit, increasing the scaling parameters $w$ and $\rho$ narrows the metastable and unstable regions. In the small-quark-mass-limit scheme, larger $w$ and $\rho$ reduce both the Ising-symmetrized pressure and density. For the conventional scheme, increasing $w$ reduces these quantities, while increasing $\rho$ raises the Ising-symmetrized pressure and has only a small effect on the density.

title: Charmed baryon decays at BESIII
abstract:
BESIII has accumulated 6.4~fb$^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ collision data at center-of-mass energies from 4.60 to 4.95~GeV, corresponding to the world's largest sample of $\Lambda_c^+ ar\Lambda_c^-$ pairs. This proceeding summarizes recent BESIII results on charmed baryon decays, including the first observation of the transverse polarization of the $\Lambda_c^+$ in $e^+e^-	o\Lambda_c^+ ar\Lambda_c^-$, a precision measurement of the inclusive decay $\Lambda_c^+	o\Lambda X$, the first observations of $\Lambda_c^+	o ne^+
u_e$ and $\Lambda_c^+	o n\pi^+\eta$ with deep-learning techniques, the first observation of $\Lambda_c^+	o pK^-e^+
u_e$ together with evidence for $\Lambda_c^+	o\Sigma^\pm\pi^\mp e^+
u_e$, and partial wave analyses of $\Lambda_c^+	o\Lambda\pi^+\eta$.

title: Flavor decomposition of electromagnetic multipole moments in $[q_1q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquarks: Light-quark analogs of $T_{cs1}(2900)^0$ with $J^P = 1^+$
abstract: We present a systematic study of the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments of compact $[q_1 q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^P = 1^+$, in the diquark--antidiquark picture and within the light-cone QCD sum rule framework. By performing a flavor decomposition across all admissible $u/d$ configurations, we show that the charm-quark contribution to the electromagnetic moments vanishes algebraically at the operator level -- a structural feature of the specific spin organization adopted here, in which the heavy antiquark resides in a pseudoscalar antidiquark, distinct from the dynamical $1/m_c$ suppression operative in alternative compact constructions and in hadronic molecules. The magnetic moments follow a coherent light-flavor pattern -- positive for $uu$-, negative for $dd$-, and suppressed for mixed-flavor diquarks -- and the quadrupole moments are non-zero throughout, corresponding, in the customary geometrical interpretation, to intrinsically deformed charge distributions. We further identify the dimensionless multipole ratio $\mathcal{D}/\mu$ as a structural observable, independent of the normalization of the interpolating current, which probes the relative geometry of the spin-current and charge distributions complementary to the absolute moments. Taken together, the algebraic decoupling of the charm contribution and the operator-level distinction it implies among different singly-heavy tetraquark architectures constitute methodological signatures that discriminate among the corresponding internal organizations and, to the extent that a physical candidate is dominated by one of them, among compact and molecular interpretations.

title: Information Geometry of DGLAP Evolution: From Geodesic Tests to Emergent Small-Circle Geometry
abstract: We investigate the geometric structure of leading-order (LO) nonsinglet DGLAP evolution on the Fisher--Rao manifold of normalized valence distributions, asking whether the QCD-selected trajectory is geodesic and how its departure from geodesic motion is organized. Through the isometric embedding $\Phi=2\sqrt{p}$, the evolution is represented as a curve on a Hilbert sphere of radius two, with its velocity and acceleration determined directly by the DGLAP operator. For a GRV98-based total-valence trajectory over $2\leq Q^2\leq 2000~{\rm GeV}^2$, we find a nonzero but weakly scale-dependent geodesic curvature. An arc-length-weighted principal-component analysis shows that two affine directions capture more than $99.999\%$ of the trajectory variance. The corresponding affine plane intersects the Fisher sphere in a small circle, whose predicted geodesic curvature closely agrees with that reconstructed from the DGLAP-generated acceleration. An $x$-resolved analysis further reveals that Fisher motion is governed by relative PDF reshaping rather than probability weight alone, with different momentum-fraction regions contributing to motion along the trajectory and its transverse bending. The Mellin representation provides a complementary perspective on the effective dimensional reduction through the collective evolution of the spectral hierarchy. These results establish a quantitative information-geometric characterization of the reference LO DGLAP trajectory and reveal an organized, near-small-circle structure over the finite evolution interval.

title: Pion chemical potentials as seen from transverse momentum distributions
abstract: We examine the transverse momentum spectra of negatively charged pions emitted in proton-proton, proton-antiproton, and nucleus-nucleus collisions at beam momenta from tens to hundreds of GeV$/c$. The measured spectra are described within the framework of nonextensive Tsallis statistics, allowing the corresponding chemical potentials to be determined through a quantitative comparison with experimental data. The extracted thermodynamic parameters are subsequently employed to explore the structure of the phase diagram in the chemical potential-temperature ($\mu$-$T$) plane, with particular emphasis on identifying possible signatures of a phase transition. Within this interpretation, pion production in the midrapidity region is associated with a phase characterized by broken chiral symmetry, whereas increasing rapidity corresponds to an evolution toward a regime in which chiral symmetry is restored.

title: From Harmonic Oscillators to Multiplicity Distributions in Particle Production Processes
abstract: We propose an oscillator framework of studying multi-particle production processes using the information theory approach. For a system of degenerate oscillators, we derive the negative binomial distribution (NBD) and its nonadditive generalization represented as gNBD. We observe that gNBD derived from nonadditive statistics describes data in higher multiplicity region, thereby providing an alternative for the multi-component distributions used in phenomenological studies. We also generalize our framework for non-degenerate oscillators and encounter a Lerch-type generalization of the Barnes zeta function that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been studied in the context of nonadditive statistics and multiplicity studies before.

title: Displaced e+e- Signatures from an X17-Mediated Inelastic Dark-Sector Cascade
abstract: We investigate displaced electron-positron signatures from an inelastic dark sector mediated by a light vector boson associated with the X17 anomaly. A heavy neutral fermion decays into a lighter stable state and the mediator, whose subsequent decay produces a single visible vertex after two stages of neutral propagation. We calculate the decay width, displacement distribution, lepton kinematics, and production rate in electro-positron collisions, including vector polarization. At Belle II, stronger dark-sector couplings increase production but require finely adjusted masses to preserve a macroscopic decay length. We quantify off-shell contributions and assess the validity of the two-body approximation. We show that the electron-positron pair cannot satisfy simultaneously the moment and opening-angle cuts of an existing search proposal for the configuration studied. Less restrictive selections allow nonzero kinematic acceptance. Our results clarify the experimental requirements for searching these signatures at Belle II.

title: Partial reconstruction of the decay $B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow \phi(K^{+}K^{-})\eta' (\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\eta)$
abstract: The decay $B_s^0 \to \phi(K^+K^-)\eta'(\pi^+\pi^-\eta)$ is of particular interest in flavour physics because in the Standard Model it proceeds predominantly through the quark transition $\bar{b} \to \bar{s}s\bar{s}$. However, the reconstruction of this decay is experimentally challenging due to the presence of the neutral $\eta$ particle, which significantly reduces the overall reconstruction efficiency. In this study, the feasibility of using the partial reconstruction technique to reconstruct the invariant mass of the $B_s^0$ meson without explicitly detecting the $\eta$ particle is investigated. Monte Carlo simulated events corresponding to an FCC-ee environment are used, and the effects of detector momentum and vertex resolutions on the reconstruction performance are examined. The results show that improved vertex resolution substantially improves the global reconstructed mass response and partial-reconstruction efficiency, while improvements in momentum resolution are manifested primarily through a narrowing of the fitted central DCB component. These findings suggest that future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders such as FCC-ee could effectively exploit the partial reconstruction technique to study rare decay modes containing undetected neutral particles.

title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
abstract: We study a two-component dark matter model in which a real singlet scalar and an inert doublet scalar are simultaneously present alongside the Standard Model, each stabilized by an independent discrete symmetry. The real singlet undergoes a strong first-order transition at high temperature, establishing an intermediate phase with a non-zero singlet vacuum expectation value, which in turn generates the barrier required for the Higgs field to complete a strongly first-order electroweak transition at a lower temperature. This two-step mechanism naturally enforces the condition $v_c/T_c \geq 1$, the sphaleron washout-avoidance criterion necessary for electroweak baryogenesis. The gravitational wave spectrum from both steps is computed; the second step produces a decihertz signal, peaking near $0.08$--$0.34~\mathrm{Hz}$ across the viable parameter space and $0.14$--$0.22~\mathrm{Hz}$ at the benchmark points, that reaches the sensitivity of DECIGO for the strongest transitions and of BBO more widely, while the first remains sub-threshold for all planned detectors. At the coupling values required to drive the phase transition, the singlet is generically underabundant as a thermal relic, so the inert doublet carries the dominant fraction of the observed relic density. Confronting the model with current constraints, we find that the LUX-ZEPLIN 2024 result excludes the entire electroweak-phase-transition-viable parameter space of the singlet sector across the full mass range, even after rescaling by the singlet relic fraction, establishing a complete no-go for the singlet as a viable thermal dark matter candidate in this framework.

title: Femtoscopic correlation functions between the lightest charmed hadrons
abstract: Femtoscopic momentum correlations probe low-energy interactions of short-lived charmed hadrons that are inaccessible to conventional scattering experiments. We calculate the correlation functions of $D^{+}D^{+}$, $D^{0}D^{0}$, $D^{+}D^{0}$, and $\Lambda_c^+\Lambda_c^+$ in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$~TeV, using species-dependent non-Gaussian PHSD sources constructed from hadronization points and strong interactions calibrated to lattice-QCD scattering lengths: OBE and EFT-contact models for $DD$, and an EFT-contact model for $\Lambda_c\Lambda_c$. Coulomb and quantum-statistical effects are included consistently. Although the calibrated interactions are weakly repulsive, the channels separate the relevant effects: $D^{+}D^{0}$, free of Coulomb distortion and identical-particle interference, gives the cleanest access to the $DD$ strong interaction, whereas $\Lambda_c^+\Lambda_c^+$ is most pronounced in peripheral collisions, where the compact source enhances the low-momentum signal. The $\Lambda_c\Lambda_c$ input is taken from lattice QCD at a nonphysical pion mass, so its physical-point shift is not quantified here. Within these stated inputs, the results provide ALICE-ready benchmark correlations and background references; the quoted bands propagate only the lattice scattering-length uncertainty.

title: Constraints on Dark Matter Annihilation from Starlight-Induced Inverse Compton Emission in Omega Centauri
abstract: The search for the particle identity of dark matter (DM) remains one of the foremost challenges in modern physics. In this work, we derive new constraints on the DM annihilation cross section $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ by considering the inverse Compton (IC) scattering of DM annihilation injected $e^+e^-$ off the starlight radiation field in Omega Centauri. As a likely remnant core of a dwarf galaxy, Omega Centauri provides a dense stellar environment that enhances the predict IC signal. Using multi-wavelength observations from Chandra and Fermi-LAT, we establish upper limits on $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ over a wide DM mass range from MeV to TeV. Notably, in the tens-of-MeV range, our results surpass existing constraints by approximately two orders of magnitude, exceeding $\langle\sigma v\rangle \sim 10^{-31}~{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At several GeV to the TeV DM masses range, our constraints also remain stronger than existing limits. Our results demonstrate that starlight induced IC emission is an important component for indirect DM searches in dense stellar systems, establishing Omega Centauri as a powerful probe of the nature of DM.

title: Information geometry of DGLAP evolution
abstract: Quark and gluon splittings shift proton momentum toward smaller fractions with increasing resolution. Momentum conservation makes the summed momentum-weighted quark and gluon densities, when nonnegative, a probability distribution. We apply information geometry, the geometry of probability distributions, to this probabilistic form of Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi evolution. We evaluate, to our knowledge for the first time, the speed at which the shape of the proton's momentum distribution changes, measured by how well distributions at neighboring resolutions can be told apart statistically. At leading order, with one-loop splitting functions and running coupling, five fixed quark flavors, nonnegative quark and gluon densities and sufficiently regular inputs, we obtain a closed-form lower bound on this speed. Once the coupling is specified, three numbers of the input (the distribution at the starting resolution) fix the bound at every scale without computing the evolved distribution. For three of the five model inputs at four scales from 2 GeV to 10 TeV, the squared bound is at least 94.8 percent of the squared speed. The bound is reached when the distribution's relative rate of change is linear in the logarithm of the inverse momentum fraction. For these three model inputs at the four scales, the relative rate of change is close to this linear form in mean square weighted by momentum.

title: Form factors and weak decays of $\Lambda_b\to\Lambda_c^*(2595)$ and $\Xi_b\to\Xi_c^*(2790)$
A Catalog of Lepton Mass Textures from Koide and Alikhanov Relations
abstract: The empirical Koide relation for charged-lepton masses and the recently proposed Alikhanov relation for neutrino mass-squared differences offer intriguing hints toward understanding the structure of lepton mass matrices. Motivated by these observations, we systematically explore charged-lepton and neutrino mass-matrix textures that satisfy these relations and confront their predictions for lepton mixing with experimental data. For the charged-lepton sector, we investigate representative positive Hermitian square-root matrices classified by the number of common eigenvector directions of their generators: three, one, or none. For the neutrino sector, an exhaustive enumeration of real symmetric integer matrices with entries between $-5$ and $5$ identifies six signed-permutation classes with $m_1=0$ and six with $m_1>0$ that satisfy the Alikhanov relation. Combining these neutrino textures with the charged-lepton constructions, allowing for different relative flavor orientations and phase alignments, yields $400$ viable structural pairs consistent with the measured lepton mixing parameters. All retained solutions satisfy the adopted cosmological bound on the sum of neutrino masses and existing laboratory constraints. In particular, the full-rank neutrino textures predict $m_1\simeq16.77$-$17.22\,\mathrm{meV}$. Representative viable solutions yield effective Majorana masses $m_{\beta\beta}\simeq1.29$-$4.03\,\mathrm{meV}$ and $4.07$-$18.67\,\mathrm{meV}$ for the $m_1=0$ and $m_1>0$ branches, respectively, providing potential targets for future high-sensitivity searches.

title: Polarization signatures of mixed scalar - pseudoscalar ALP - photon couplings in intense laser pulses
abstract: We investigate photon-to-axion-like-particle (ALP) conversion in a finite, linearly polarized laser pulse for a single ALP field with simultaneous scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type couplings to photons. Varying the collision angle between the strong pulse and the probe provides a continuous kinematic scan of the resonant ALP mass. For fixed kinematics in this setting, the scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type ALP conversion amplitudes interfere coherently, making both the photon-to-ALP conversion probability and the polarization rotation depend on the difference between the probe polarization angle $\alpha$ and the coupling angle $\theta_g$. Conversion is maximal at $|\alpha-\theta_g|=90^\circ$, where the polarization rotation vanishes, while the rotation magnitude peaks at $\alpha-\theta_g=45^\circ$ modulo $90^\circ$, where conversion is half-maximal. These complementary polarization-angle dependences provide polarization-resolved signatures of mixed scalar--pseudoscalar photon couplings.

title: Probing the $\tau$ anomalous magnetic and electric dipole moments in photon-induced $\gamma\gamma\to\tau^+\tau^-$ production at the FCC-hh
abstract: The sensitivity of the FCC-hh to the anomalous magnetic moment $a_\tau$ and the electric dipole moment $d_\tau$ of the $\tau$ lepton is studied in photon-induced $\gamma\gamma\to\tau^+\tau^-$ production with both $\tau$ leptons decaying hadronically. Central exclusive (elastic) signal events, in which both protons remain intact, are generated with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO using a FeynRules UFO model of the anomalous $\gamma\tau\tau$ vertex merged with the TauDecay model, so that the $\tau$ decays and their spin correlations are included in the matrix element. Single- and double-dissociative production is estimated with SuperChic and added to the elastic signal with its own coupling dependence and with normalisation and shape uncertainties of 25%. Pythia 8 decays the unstable hadrons in the signal, decays the $\tau$ leptons and simulates the parton shower and hadronisation in the backgrounds, and hadronises the dissociated protons. Signal and backgrounds are passed through the Delphes simulation of the FCC-hh detector. Hadronic $\tau$ decays are reconstructed from particle-flow tracks and photons with an algorithm based on the hadrons-plus-strips approach, with an efficiency of 73.4% within the acceptance. Requiring no additional tracks from the $\tau$ vertices retains part of the dissociative contribution and reduces the Drell-Yan and $\gamma\gamma\to WW$ backgrounds to 0.9% of the SM yield. The couplings are constrained from the shape of the total transverse mass distribution. For a centre-of-mass energy of 84 TeV and 30 ab$^{-1}$, the expected 95% CL limits are $-3.38\times10^{-4} < a_\tau < 3.36\times10^{-4}$ and $|d_\tau| < 1.88\times10^{-18}\,e\,$cm, about an order of magnitude beyond the current bounds. Results are also given for FCC-hh scenarios between 72 and 120 TeV and for an optimistic detector parametrisation.

title: Pulse Shape Model for a Light Enhanced Phonon Detector
abstract: COSINUS has tested prototype NaI-based cryogenic scintillating calorimeters with a composite design, in which the transition edge sensor (TES) is fabricated on a separate carrier crystal coupled to the NaI target. Measurements with the composite detectors showed deviations from the known pulse shape description for cryogenic calorimeters and did not reveal an identifiable nuclear recoil population during a neutron calibration. In this work we present a new pulse shape model which provides an explanation to these observations and that laid the foundation for the development of the final COSINUS phonon detector design named remote TES (remoTES). We demonstrate that the first COSINUS detector prototypes featured a phonon channel with signal enhancement by light absorption in the carrier, namely a light enhanced phonon detector. This design offers for the first time the chance to use a single channel phonon detector for particle discrimination. We present recent results using a novel pulse shape fitting method based on the Bayesian inference software package BAT.jl.

title: Soft Breaking Naturalness in Majorana Fermion Loop induced Scalar and Majoron Amplitudes
abstract: Majorana fermion loops contribute a shift-symmetry violating effective potential to the coupled scalar field. When the Majorana fermion is light, a larger number of symmetry violating insertions let the loop contribution to grow increasingly infrared sensitive to the Majorana mass. With explicit calculations, we calculate the symmetry violating amplitudes, show that the scalar potential's natural scales serve as nonzero kinematic matching points which remove the superficial sensitivity to the symmetry-violating Majorana mass, continuously restoring the shift symmetry in agreement with 't Hooft naturalness. In the spontaneous broken phase, the scalar radial vacuum expectation value readily ensures the infrared safety of symmetry violating Majorana fermion loops, and all $n$-point Majoron functions develop a leading linear dependence on the symmetry violating parameter in the soft breaking limit, which matches the expansion of the Coleman-Weinberg determinant.

title: Hadronization in QCD and Fragmentation Functions
abstract: The hadronization of quarks and gluons is reviewed within the framework of collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions closely associated with the notion of factorization in hard scattering processes in QCD. The state-of-the-art in calculating both the scale evolution of fragmentation functions and the partonic cross sections pertinent to their determination from data up to next-to-next-to-leading order accuracy is presented. Potential improvements up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic order are outlined as well. All relevant experimental data sets for single-inclusive pion, kaon, and unidentified charged hadron production are listed. The most recent sets of fragmentation functions and their uncertainties extracted from these data in global QCD analyses utilizing various different strategies are presented and compared to each other.

title: Likelihood-Based Confidence Curves for Bounded Parameters
abstract: When a parameter is bounded, the likelihood ratio statistic does not generally follow the chi-square limit distribution of Wilks' theorem. In fact, its asymptotic null distribution depends on the distance from the null value to the boundary, interpolating between the chi-bar-square law on the boundary and the chi-square law in the deep interior of the parameter space. We derive this distribution and use it to construct confidence curves, which are nested collections of two-sided confidence intervals or regions, for bounded parameters. We extend the existing result for the scalar parameter to a two-dimensional parameter with one or both components bounded. As the bivariate distributions are integrals of normal distributions, which are not reducible to standard statistical functions, we also give a simpler approximated distribution obtained by moment-matching. We illustrate the methods on a canonical analysis from high-energy physics, namely the Poisson signal-plus-background experiment.

title: Probing a heavy neutral lepton in a radiative neutrino model at a muon collider
abstract:
We investigate direct and Higgs-mediated production of a Dirac heavy neutral lepton in a radiative neutrino-mass model at a future $3~\mathrm{TeV}$ muon collider. We consider heavy neutral lepton masses in the window $m_Z<m_N<m_h$, where the decays $N	o\ell W$ and $N	o
u Z$ can proceed with on-shell weak bosons. We consider both direct production, $\mu^+\mu^-	o N
u$, and Higgs-mediated production through $\mu^+\mu^-	o
u_\mu ar
u_\mu h$, $h	o N
u$. Both channels lead to the common $\ell^\pm jj+p_{\mathrm T}^{\mathrm{miss}}$ final state. We perform a detector-level analysis with an integrated luminosity of $1~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, assuming unpolarized muon beams, and derive median expected $95\%$ confidence-level upper limits on the visible signal cross section ranging from approximately $0.027$ to $0.113~\mathrm{fb}$, corresponding to limits on the mixing strength parameter $|U_{\mu N}|^2$ ranging from $6.7	imes10^{-6}$ to $8.3	imes10^{-5}$ for six benchmark points. The Higgs-mediated production channel contributes $\sim15$--$72\%$ of the signal after the common event selection, but improves the expected limits by $\sim0.18$--$1.19\%$ within the common classifier and binning scheme. This small improvement reflects the classifier-score distribution of the Higgs-mediated events. The limits on $|U_{\mu N}|^2$ account for the benchmark-specific flavor mixings and assume an independent $10\%$ background uncertainty in each classifier-score bin.

title: $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $S_3$ gaugings of $\mathbb{Z}_N\times\mathbb{Z}'_N$ non-invertible symmetries: quark texture zeros and phenomenology
abstract: We investigate texture zeros in the quark Yukawa matrices arising from the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $S_3$ gauging of $\mathbb{Z}_N\times\mathbb{Z}'_N$, associated with the non-invertible $\Delta(3N^2)$ and $\Delta(6N^2)$ symmetries, respectively. We construct the equivalence classes and their fusion rules and use them as selection rules for the Yukawa interactions. We systematically classify the full-rank quark Yukawa textures generated by the two gaugings for $N=2,3,4,$ and $5$. The two gaugings yield the same texture spectrum for $N=2$ and $N=4$, whereas the $S_3$ gauging produces additional textures for $N=3$ and $N=5$. We further analyze the most restrictive texture pairs compatible with quark data and find that there are at most nine zeros in these texture pairs. For up- and down-quark mass matrices with a total of nine texture zeros, one sector is allowed to contain six zeros while the other contains three, or one contains five zeros while the other contains four. The former case has been studied in previous works. We perform numerical fits for the latter and find it consistent with experimental data. Some viable textures also admit real quark-mass determinants while retaining a physical CKM phase, suggesting a possible connection to the strong CP problem.

title: Automation of amplitude-level QED resummation with ACRAIC
abstract: Precision electroweak predictions for future $e^+e^-$ colliders will require levels of precision unmatched in collider physics and the modelling of multiple-photon emissions, and the exponentiation of the associated logarithms needs to be carefully considered. The Yennie-Frautschi-Suura theorem subtracts the infrared singularities to all orders and exponentiates them, leaving infrared-finite remainders which can be calculated order-by-order. Coherent exponentiation performs this subtraction at the amplitude level, preserving the interference between emissions, but has so far been available only for fermion-pair production, with hand-coded amplitudes. We present ACRAIC, an automated, amplitude-level realization of this subtraction for general scattering processes in Sherpa. This method allows us to construct an $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ amplitude level subtraction scheme, in which the infrared-finite remainders are tree-level helicity amplitudes with partition-dependent propagator shifts, computed by the Berends--Giele recursion, and the one-loop electroweak virtual enters through a per-helicity factor from the loop provider. At $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ two independent matchings agree on the size of the missing higher orders to $\sim10^{-3}$, and the estimated perturbative uncertainty shrinks by about an order of magnitude relative to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$.

title: Holographic Calculation of Semileptonic Form Factors and the Isgur--Wise Function for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ Decays
abstract: We present a holographic analysis of the semileptonic decays $B \to D \ell \bar{\nu}_\ell$ and $B_s \to D_s \ell \bar{\nu}_\ell$ within the Softwall Model (SWM) and the Non-Quadratic Softwall Model (NQSWM). We extract the Isgur-Wise function from the overlap integral of bulk wavefunctions, with model parameters fixed by the heavy-light meson spectra. We impose Heavy Quark Symmetry (HQS) at zero recoil and address the apparent paradox of a non-conserved electroweak current dual to a massless bulk vector field. We argue that the non-conservation, arising from explicit flavor-- symmetry breaking by quark masses, does not generate an anomalous dimension. Hence the bulk field remains massless, and the non-conservation is \emph{encoded} in the independent boundary couplings $g_+$ and $g_-$. Our predictions for the branching fractions are in good agreement with LHCb data for $B_s \to D_s$ decays. The lepton-flavor universality ratios $R(D)$ and $R(D_s)$ are consistent with Standard Model and lattice QCD predictions. We find that the holographic models reproduce the universality of the Isgur-Wise function near zero recoil, while discrepancies at maximum recoil suggest that a more complete treatment of higher-order $1/m_Q$ corrections is needed.

title: Open Science with the LHCb Ntupling Service
authors: Daan Eduard Rosendal (Now at Lakera company
abstract: The data samples collected at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN are highly valuable, and the analysis of these data has led to numerous discoveries and the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. Preserving and providing open access to these data for future analysts is imperative to maximize the scientific output of the collected data. The LHCb collaboration has developed a novel approach to this pursuit of open science, the LHCb Ntupling Service: a web service for on-demand production and publishing of custom LHCb open data, providing open access to both Run 1, and for the first time, Run 2 proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment, amounting to over 4 PB of data to explore.

title: Four-loop electron EDM matching and timelike $\tau$ electric dipole form factor
abstract: We compute the four-loop matching of a CP-odd four-$\tau$ interaction onto the electron electric dipole moment (EDM), together with the leading timelike $\tau$ dipole form factor generated by the same source. Both results are scale independent at this order. Without a local electron dipole, exact electron-EDM cancellation still leaves a timelike $\tau$ signal proportional to the four-$\tau$ coefficient. Its absorptive part cannot be canceled by a real local dipole, allowing collider limits to constrain the cancellation direction and complement static electron-EDM searches.

title: Hybrid Stars with Different Amount of Quark Matter
abstract: In a previous work, we explored the possibility of neutron stars with large quark cores. Through Bayesian inference, we obtained large sets of equations of state imposing constraints regarding the properties of nuclear matter, mass-radius data from NICER, the GW170817 data from Virgo-LIGO collaboration, perturbative QCD and causality. We also imposed that the maximum mass neutron star (NS$\text{max}$) must have a large quark core. In this work, we obtain a new set of equations of state (SmallQ set) with the same constraints as before. However, we relaxed the last constraint, imposing only that NS$\text{max}$ must have quark core, regardless of its size. We compare the results with the set from our previous paper constrained by NICER and GW170817 observations NJL-GW. For both sets, we use the Relativistic Mean Field model with nonlinear meson interactions for the hadron phase and the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model with four- and eight-quark interaction terms for the quark phase. The SmallQ set has higher values of phase transition density, with 3 -- 4.5 $\rho_0$, compared to the NJL-GW, with 2 -- 2.5 $\rho_0$. The new set describes NSs with smaller radius and smaller tidal deformability, and is more compatible with NICER and GW170817 data. A difference in the quark matter composition is observed, with a larger quark strange fraction occurring in the SmallQ set. Within this set, $2 M_\odot$ NSs may contain little to no quark matter. It is shown that there is a non negligible fraction of EOS whose mass-radius curve presents a positive slope for 1.8 $M_\odot$ stars, while for nucleonic stars this fraction is negligible and for hyperonic stars the slope is always negative.

title: Magnetic-field dependence of the QCD electric screening mass parameter through $g^4$ in hot and dense matter
abstract: A constant magnetic field modifies the hard electric screening sector of hot and dense QCD and generates a directional splitting at $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$. We determine the strict-hard screening pole through $g^4$ for three massless flavors with physical $u,d,s$ charges, retaining the full $eB/T^2$ dependence without a weak- or strong-field expansion. The shifted-frequency construction used for the two-loop exchange contribution is a background-field Feynman-gauge curvature; we derive and apply its local conversion to the ordinary Feynman-gauge self-energy before assembling the screening pole. The leading magnetic shift is isotropic, while the $g^4$ directional splitting arises from the one-loop anisotropic kinetic normalization; the symmetry-allowed finite-density $A_0F_{12}$ mixing is numerically small over the studied range for physical $u,d,s$ charges. For $\mu/T=0$ and $1$, the magnetic $g^4$ coefficient is positive over $0\le eB/T^2\le4$ and is strongly reduced by density. Extending the calculation to $0\le\mu/T\le2$ at $eB/T^2=1$ and $4$ reveals sign reversals of both the leading magnetic coefficient and the directional splitting at sufficiently large density. The zero-field limit reproduces the Braaten-Nieto result and its finite-density extension by Vuorinen. The running coupling used only for the phenomenological magnetic mass shift is chosen independently of $B$, so that all magnetic-field dependence through $g^4$ resides in the calculated coefficients.

title: Blueprint for an AI-Enabled Particle Theory Community
authors: George T. Fleming (Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory)
Daniel C. Hackett (Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory)
Can Kilic (University of Texas at Austin)
Tim M. P. Tait (University of California
abstract: Rapid advances in the capabilities and reach of artificial intelligence (AI) are changing research in particle physics. In this new era, AI is an innovative tool for theoretical physicists, while the interaction of AI and particle theory is itself a developing field. We argue that particle theory requires a community-scale effort to realize its full potential. We show how particle theory occupies a unique position in the AI for physics landscape, and describe the complementarity of AI and theory developments. We conclude with a series of recommendations on how to build an AI-enabled theory community for the Genesis Mission.

title: Isospin breaking in $\rho\pi\pi$ couplings: $\rho^{+,0}$ width difference and muon $g-2$
abstract: The dominant contribution to the hadronic vaccum polarization (HVP) of the muon $g-2$ can be calculated using the hadronic spectrum in $\tau^- \to \pi^-\pi^0\nu_{\tau}$ decay, provided isospin breaking (IB) corrections are properly accounted for. Among these corrections, IB in the $\rho\pi\pi$ coupling has been pointed out as a missing ingredient. In this work, we calculate this IB effect within the impulse approximation using a symmetry-preserving framework based on Dyson-Schwinger and Bethe-Salpeter equations, incorporating fully dressed quark propagators and meson Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes. We then estimate its effect in the HVP contribution to the muon $g-2$. As a natural extension, we also compute the IB in the ratio of $\phi K^+K^-/\phi K^0\bar{K^0}$ couplings and compare with existing data. We obtain a coupling ratio $g_{\rho^0\pi^+\pi^-}/g_{\rho^+\pi^+\pi^0} = 1.0024(17)(1)$, which yields an isospin-breaking correction of $\Delta a_\mu^{\mathrm{HVP,LO}}[\rho\pi\pi] = -2.32(1.64)\times 10^{-10}$ to the two-pion contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment extracted from $\tau$ decay data.

title: MadStree: automated evaluation of tree-level de Sitter correlators
abstract: We first derived the formulae of recursive reduction and dlog-form differential equations for arbitrary tree-level cosmological correlator, taking the external relations of massless bulk propagators into consideration. The differential equations could be systematically solved and provide the efficient evaluation of them. We have implemented this methodology as a user-friendly Mathematica package MadStree for computing arbitrary tree-level cosmological correlators.
